steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).

Place bacon in a large, deep skillet. Cook over medium-high heat until evenly brown. Drain, but reserve 1 tablespoon of grease. Crumble bacon and set aside. Heat reserved bacon grease in a skillet and sauté onion until soft.
In a large bowl, beat together eggs, milk, flour, parsley, thyme, salt, and pepper. Add bacon, onion, mozzarella, and Cheddar cheese; mix well. Pour mixture into pie crust.
Bake in the preheated oven for 45 minutes, or until lightly brown on top and firm in the middle. Serve warm.

raw_recipe.headline: Country Quiche
raw_recipe.description: A classic quiche Lorraine with bacon, onions, eggs, and cheese.

review.reviewBody: I doubled this recipe and put it in 2 deep dish pie shells that I baked for about 8 minutes at 400 degrees, although I think regular depth would work too. I used 2 cups of cheddar cheese for the double recipe, and about 8 oz. of chopped brocolli. I also used onion powder instead of onion, because I was low on time. With the brocolli, 4 pieces of bacon was plenty per quiche. Unless you really like the herbs, they were not necessary. It's a good basic recipe that I will use again.

Made this the other day. First, I have made a LOT of quiche and have never seen one that called for flour. I did follow the recipe as written & the flavor was ok. However, it did not make enough to fill a deep dish shell. It turned out flat and dry. Mixing the bacon, onion & cheeses into the egg was a mistake. I ended up having to use a fork to redistribute them. Plus, recipe called for too much baking time. It was completely done in just 30 min. I ended up having to put it under the broiler of my toaster oven to brown the crust. Next time I'll make some changes. 1) no flour; 2) 6 eggs instead of 4; 3) 3/4 cup of both cheeses instead of 1/2 cup of each; 4) 1/4 cup of heavy cream + 1/4 cup milk to make it richer. At some point if I want it with a little bite, I'll substitute pepper jack for the mozzarella.

This recipe tastes great, but something is wrong with the ingredient measurements and with the cooking time. I found an almost identical recipe that uses 1.5 cups of milk and .5 cup of flour. It instructs to put the bacon, onion, and the cheeses on the crust before pouring in the egg mixure. It also bakes the quiche for 35 minutes. I plan to make this again with the modifications and, hopefully, change my rating.

I am actually cooking off two of these quiches as we speak. I did change things up a little based on the reviews. I added 4 oz of low fat ricotta cheese, omitted the bacon, added 1 bunch of swiss chard to the first quiche and 1 bunch of kale to the second quiche. For both the chard and the kale, I wilted them down as I was doing the onions. I am really looking forward to having some of this tomorrow morning :)

This recipe is very tasty however the first time it turned out too dry.
Best option is to use 3 Tablespoons of milk and only 1 Tablespoon of flour. Cook for only 30mins at 350 degrees and it turns out perfectly!!
Enjoy!
Used my homemade crust (1 C flour, 1/4 c butter, 1 - 3 TBSP of cold milk) and came out fantastic for Christmas brunch, even meat eating men loved it :)

I had some pie crust I made before sitting in my freezer to use so I decided it was quiche time. I used this recipe as more of a guide, in that I used a half pound of bacon instead of counting out 8 slices, about a cup and a half of frozen broccoli that I sautéed with the onions, everything that looked good in my spice cabinet, and a quarter cup of pepperjack instead of mozzarella cheese. I also generously sprinkled parmesan cheese over the top. It turned out fabulously. The entire quiche was eatten by 3 adults and 2 children in one night! I’m definitely making this again.

Very easy and delicious. I followed other suggestions and baked the empty crust for about 10 minutes. I also added a little extra mozzarella and about 3/4 chopped fresh broccoli which I cooked in a little bacon grease for a few minutes. I will definitely make it again!
It was dry and heavy and had a heavy onion flavor. After I changed the recipe to 1/3c onion, 1c half & half, no flour, no thyme, and 1+1/2 c grated Swiss, it was delicious! Light and fluffy.

I used a deep dish pie shell and doubled the recipe. I hadn't intended to, but the first shell was pre-baked too much and fell apart. 

I also bought pre-cooked bacon, diced it up and threw it in the pan with the onion I had started sautéing in the pan with Kerrygold Butter.

I followed the rest of the recipe. It was delicious and a hit with the people I worked the elections with.

I like to double the recipe, add a pound of browned onion sausage, and pour into two pie crusts. I have also added a jar of drained mushrooms if I have them on hand. This is one of my husband's favorite dishes because it heats up well for breakfast the next day! I like it because it freezes well.
Easy!!

Really good! Really simple. I made as written except doubled and it was just right. I used Wild Fork Applewood Bacon Steaks, da bomb-diggity. I'd say this is more like Egg Pie than quiche. It's kinda heavy to be called quiche. Will definitely be making this again.

We'll see! It just came out of the oven! I adjusted some ingredients based on my pantry, (sage sausage instead of bacon and green onions instead of white or yellow). Update to come with review! UPDATE: This was awesome!! Quick easy and delicious. It's very "adjustable" to your pantry, a perfect canvas so to speak😉
Really easy recipe to follow. Came out perfect! Next time I will add another egg. Delicious!
use this as my base for all quiche. make it all the time bacon, ham, veggies it all works
Why only 2 tablespoons of milk, it was very dry.
I like sour cream for a richer flavor!
This recipe was a hit!

This cooked up dry, firm, and nothing like a real quiche. No moist, fluffy creaminess. I should have known because there is no evaporated milk or cream in the recipe, but it got good reviews so I thought I would try it. We threw it out.
